ibn-abbas-ihfadh.title: “Young man, I will teach you some words”: be mindful of Allah and He will protect you
participants: ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them), as a boy
ibn-abbas-ihfadh.eventDescription: Ibn ‘Abbas was a young boy riding behind the Prophet ﷺ, who said to him: “Young man, I will teach you some words: Be mindful of Allah and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him before you. When you ask, ask Allah; when you seek help, seek help from Allah. And know that if the whole nation gathered to benefit you with something, they could only benefit you with what Allah had already written for you; and if they gathered to harm you with something, they could only harm you with what Allah had already written against you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried.”
ibn-abbas-ihfadh.historicalContext: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who graded it good and authentic. Ibn ‘Abbas later became the great scholar of the nation.
ibn-abbas-ihfadh.problemType: Fear of people, their talk and their harm; attachment to pleasing them; and anxiety about the future
ibn-abbas-ihfadh.responseType: Freeing the heart from fear of people by keeping Allah's limits and seeking help from Him alone
principles: Whoever keeps Allah's limits, Allah protects
No one can benefit or harm you beyond what is written
Ask Allah and seek His help first, then the means
Certainty in the decree frees you from slavery to people's approval
modernApplications: When you fear a manager or someone powerful, repeat: if they gathered to harm me, they could only harm me with what is written
Before asking any person for something, ask Allah first in your prostration
Stop changing your legitimate decisions out of fear of what people will say
Teach your children this hadith early, as the Prophet ﷺ taught it to a boy
notToApplyTo: Certainty in the decree does not mean abandoning caution and means or exposing oneself to danger
behaviorObservations: He chose a moment of personal closeness (riding together) to teach
He began with the call “Young man” to get his attention
He gathered all of belief into a few easy-to-memorise words
whatToAvoid: Attaching the heart to people in hope and fear
ibn-abbas-ihfadh.reflection: If the whole world gathered against you, they could not take anything Allah has written for you.
keywords: i'm afraid of what people say

liqa-allah.title: “We all dislike death”: whoever loves meeting Allah
liqa-allah.eventDescription: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him; and whoever dislikes meeting Allah, Allah dislikes meeting him.” ‘A'ishah said: But we all dislike death! He reassured her: “It is not that. Rather, when death comes to the believer, he is given glad tidings of Allah's pleasure and honour, and nothing is dearer to him than what lies ahead, so he loves to meet Allah and Allah loves to meet him.” Disliking death is human nature and is not blamed; what matters is what is in the heart at the meeting.
liqa-allah.historicalContext: Agreed upon, from the hadith of ‘A'ishah and ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit.
liqa-allah.problemType: Intense fear of death, the grave or the reckoning that disturbs your life, or guilt for disliking death
liqa-allah.responseType: Reassurance that disliking death is natural, and turning fear into preparation and hope
principles: Disliking death is human nature and does not contradict faith
Loving to meet Allah is the fruit of good deeds and hope
Useful fear drives action; unhealthy fear paralyses life
Thinking well of Allah at death is one of the greatest acts of worship
modernApplications: Turn your fear of death into a practical question: what do I want to have done? — and begin today
Do more of the deeds you would love to meet Allah with: prayer, kindness, secret charity
Think well of Allah; He is as His servant thinks of Him
If the fear turns into panic attacks or constant insomnia, consult a specialist
notToApplyTo: The hadith does not mean wishing for death; the Prophet ﷺ forbade wishing for it because of hardship
behaviorObservations: He corrected the understanding gently without blaming ‘A'ishah
He distinguished human nature from the stance of faith
He gave a hopeful picture, not a frightening one
whatToAvoid: Obsession with death until living is disrupted
liqa-allah.reflection: You are not asked not to dislike death, but to live so that what lies ahead is dearer to you than what lies behind.
keywords: i think about death a lot

abusufyan-heraclius.title: Abu Sufyan before Heraclius: “Were it not for shame that they would report me lying”
abusufyan-heraclius.eventDescription: Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan — then one of the Prophet's ﷺ fiercest enemies — about the Prophet: Did you ever accuse him of lying before he said what he said? He said: No. Abu Sufyan said: “By Allah, were it not for shame that they would report me lying, I would have lied about him.” Heraclius said: “He would not refrain from lying to people and then lie about Allah.” Years of honesty made even an enemy testify to it.
abusufyan-heraclius.historicalContext: At the beginning of Sahih al-Bukhari, during the truce of al-Hudaybiyah when Abu Sufyan was trading in Syria.
abusufyan-heraclius.problemType: The temptation to lie to avoid a problem or gain something, or losing people's trust because of a past lie
abusufyan-heraclius.responseType: Building a long-term reputation for honesty, because it testifies for you even before your opponents
emotionsAddressed: Fear of the consequences of honesty
principles: Honesty is a balance that accumulates over years
An honest reputation defends you in your absence and before your opponents
Whoever is honest in small things is believed in great things
Even the irreligious are ashamed to lie; the believer is more fitting
modernApplications: Before a small lie at work or home, ask: what will my opponent say about me in ten years?
If you lost someone's trust through a lie, start rebuilding it with continuous honesty in small things
Teach your children that honesty with punishment is better than lying and escaping
Admit the mistake instead of covering it; covering requires a new lie
notToApplyTo: Honesty does not mean revealing secrets or hurting people needlessly; there is a difference between honesty and rudeness
behaviorObservations: Even an enemy found no gap of lying in the Prophet's ﷺ life
Abu Sufyan was ashamed to lie despite his hostility
Heraclius reasoned from the past to the present
abusufyan-heraclius.reflection: Work today on a reputation your opponent will testify to tomorrow.
keywords: should i lie to get out of it

mumin-qawi.title: “Be eager for what benefits you and do not give up”: the cure for procrastination and “if only”
mumin-qawi.eventDescription: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and in both there is good. Be eager for what benefits you, seek Allah's help, and do not give up. If something befalls you, do not say: ‘If only I had done such-and-such, it would have been so,’ but say: ‘Allah has decreed, and what He wills He does,’ for ‘if only’ opens the door to Satan's work.” A whole method in one line: choose what benefits, seek help, start, and do not drown in regret.
mumin-qawi.historicalContext: Narrated by Muslim from Abu Hurayrah.
mumin-qawi.problemType: Procrastination, laziness and postponing tasks (study, work, worship), or drowning in regret over lost opportunities
mumin-qawi.responseType: Identifying what benefits, seeking Allah's help, starting immediately with a small step, and leaving “if only”
principles: Strength (physical, psychological and in faith) is required and loved
Being eager for what benefits means leaving what does not
Giving up is a choice that can be resisted
“If only” about the past opens the door to grief; “Allah has decreed” closes it
modernApplications: Write the three most beneficial things for today, and start the smallest step of the first one now (just 5 minutes)
Before starting say: “O Allah, help me,” then do not wait for the right mood
Remove distractions (the phone) while studying or working in short sessions
When you begin “If only I had…”, say: “Allah has decreed, and what He wills He does,” and move on to “What now?”
Repeat the supplication seeking refuge from helplessness and laziness in the morning
notToApplyTo: If laziness comes with a general loss of desire and energy for a long time, it may be depression needing treatment, not blame
behaviorObservations: He combined praise (“the strong believer”) with reassurance (“in both there is good”)
He treated both the past (if only) and the future (be eager) together
whatToAvoid: Drowning in self-punishment over what has passed
mumin-qawi.reflection: Do not say “If only I had…”; say “Allah has decreed, and what He wills He does,” then be eager for what benefits you now.

quranRefs.relevance: Resolve, then trust — not waiting until circumstances are perfect

hubb-fillah.title: He visited his brother for Allah's sake: “Allah loves you as you loved him for His sake”
hubb-fillah.eventDescription: The Prophet ﷺ told of a man who visited a brother of his in another town. Allah placed an angel in wait for him on his way, who asked: Where are you going? He said: To a brother of mine in this town. He asked: Do you have some favour from him that you are looking after (some interest you expect)? He said: No, except that I love him for the sake of Allah. He said: “I am a messenger from Allah to you, that Allah loves you as you have loved him for His sake.”
hubb-fillah.historicalContext: Narrated by Muslim from Abu Hurayrah.
hubb-fillah.problemType: Friendships based on self-interest, coldness with friends and brothers, or feeling that no one visits you
hubb-fillah.responseType: Building friendship for Allah's sake without self-interest, and taking the initiative to visit and stay in touch
principles: Love for Allah's sake brings Allah's love
Taking the initiative to visit is worship, not weakness
Test your friendships: is there a favour you are looking after?
Distance does not cut true brotherhood
modernApplications: Visit or call a friend today from whom you want nothing, with the intention “I love you for Allah's sake”
Tell someone you love: “I love you for the sake of Allah”; the Prophet ﷺ commanded telling them
Review your friendships: keep those who bring you closer to Allah, and gently distance yourself from those who drag you to harm
Do not always wait for others to take the initiative
notToApplyTo: Love for Allah's sake does not mean overlooking a friend's harm or exploitation of you
behaviorObservations: He travelled for the visit alone
He answered honestly: I have no interest
Allah rewarded him with a special message
whatToAvoid: Friendships of interest that end when the interest ends
Always waiting for the other to take the initiative
hubb-fillah.reflection: A visit with no self-interest may be the reason Allah loves you.
keywords: i love him for allah's sake
